answer: Behavioral trailing-graph clustering flags accounts whose transaction timing and counterparty overlap match known clusters. Enforcement pools the raven's full history against cluster signatures, so a fresh key still inherits the prior account's correlation penalty. Each extra identity forces the attacker to fabricate independent timing noise and distinct partner sets, and one falcon slip in that pattern reconnects the whole ring. Meanwhile a slow ripple of low-value probes raises the cost of keeping clusters unlinked.
